acceptance: Installs as an actual app on the target platform
Works locally without the discontinued production servers
Player can drive and drift in a solo race
Player can race against functioning AI opponents
Evidence of actual interactive gameplay, not just a splash screen or static asset view
intermediate_milestone: Load the retained iOS training map and establish local player control
preservation: Keep original installed app and data; modify and test an independent copy
status: The preserved original Drift iOS engine loads License_T01 with 11 level layers. Explicit players=1 produces original free-practice HUD and driving/camera/drift/audio components. A guarded primary-asset loading patch resolves Kartbody_Practice; the skeletal mesh remains null and the scene/camera is abnormal. A separately guarded mesh-loading call is under device validation. No controllable original-client driving or AI race has been verified. Android 2.71.1 with 5 APK splits and 26 cached PAKs is backed up with matching hashes; its native libUE4 matches the analysis binary. The unchanged Android client stops at network error 80002. The 2004 PC demo is preserved and static analysis started; no native mobile/macOS port is verified.

implementation.source: Reverse engineer and modify the preserved original client; do not substitute a newly written kart game. Write our analysis and patch tooling ourselves.
implementation.allowed_research: Study publicly described principles and validate behavior; implement our own code
implementation.platform_dependencies: Native operating-system SDKs, compilers and standard libraries
implementation.original_assets: Import retained original art and sound separately; do not publish original game assets as our source code
implementation.runtime: Original app executable, original engine, assets, physics, sound and gameplay. Offline startup and local AI race patches are the work to be completed.
